He teaches at Marist University.Explore more on these topicsUSAUS sportsMauricio PochettinocommentShareReuse this content

title: LAFC co-managing owner Larry Berg voted as next MLS commissioner | MLS | The Guardian
description: Berg, a senior partner at private equity firm 26North, will succeed Don Garber as commissioner in 2027
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: Berg, a senior partner at private equity firm 26North, will succeed Don Garber as commissioner in 2027
Content: Larry Berg celebrating the 2024 US Open Cup win with LAFC.Photograph: Shaun Clark/ISI Photos/USSF/Getty Images for USSFView image in fullscreenLarry Berg celebrating the 2024 US Open Cup win with LAFC.Photograph: Shaun Clark/ISI Photos/USSF/Getty Images for USSFMLSLAFC co-managing owner Larry Berg voted as next MLS commissionerBerg is a senior partner at private equity firm 26NorthCommissioner will take over on 1 January 2027Jeff Rueter,Alexander Abnosin New York, andPablo Iglesias MaurerMon 3 Aug 2026 16.23 EDTLast modified on Mon 3 Aug 2026 18.32 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe Major League Soccer board of governors has voted to install Los Angeles FC co-managing owner Larry Berg as the league’s next commissioner.Berg will succeed Don Garber as the head of the 30-year-old league, with a term starting on 1 January 2027. He will be the third commissioner inMLShistory.Garber, who has served as commissioner since 1999, has a contract with the league that runs until the end of 2027. The league announced Monday that he will transition to the role of chairman after Berg assumes the role, to ensure “a seamless leadership transition as MLS enters one of the most significant periods in its history”.Berg is required to divest his shares of LAFC as part of the transition process, the league said.The vote took place among all MLS owners on Monday at the league’s headquarters in midtown Manhattan in a closed-door meeting, after presentations given by Berg and David Nathanson, the other candidate for the post, earlier in the day. Nathanson’s background was largely in sports media. He spent significant time working for Fox, while also investing in the Seattle Sounders, Angel City FC (NWSL) and the Seattle Kraken (NHL).Berg comes from a private equity investment background. He is a senior adviser at 26North and was previously a partner at Apollo Global Management and the chair of McGraw-Hill Education. He initially invested as a limited partner when LAFC was launched in 2014 and became one of the club’s managing owners in 2016 after an internal buyout. He is the co-chair of MLS’s sporting and competition committee.LAFC first took the field in 2018 with former US manager Bob Bradley as coach and then-Mexico international Carlos Vela as headliner. The club quickly became one of the league’s model operations, perennial contenders on the pitch and a respected operation in many other departments. Sporting director John Thorrington, one of the club’s first hires, was named MLS sporting executive of the year in 2024, while LAFC was named the Operations Club of the Year in 2023.The club has consistently been among the league’s most valuable franchises since debuting, with Forbes estimating a valuation of$1.32bnas of May. Berg’s experience of building a well-supported club in a major market will be crucial as MLS tries to make greater inroads in other cities, such as New York and Chicago. As commissioner, he will take cues from all of MLS’s owners, including those in smaller markets who haven’t historically invested in their rosters to the extent that LAFC have.“Having worked closely with Larry over the past decade, I’ve seen first-hand the qualities that make him an exceptional leader, and I have complete confidence he is the right person to serve as Major League Soccer’s next Commissioner,” Garber said in a written statement. “I look forward to working alongside Larry during this transition and supporting him as he leads MLS into its next chapter.”Berg has been a vocal supporter of MLS’s trajectory, stating in February 2020 that he believes MLS would “pass baseball and hockey to be the No 3 sport in the US behind football and basketball” by the end of the current decade. He cited the league’s burgeoning academy system as evidence, as well as the intrinsic pull of living in the United States.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Preview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I think we’re already a league of choice to a certain extent,” Berg continued in that 2020 media day interview, “but whether we can be a top-five league or top-three league will really come down at the end of the day to money and our ability to compete for players.”The most prominent example of an American sports commissioner who had team-owner experience was Bud Selig, who owned the Milwaukee Brewers before becoming Major League Baseball’s lead executive in 1992, although he was initially appointed on an acting basis.Berg is listed on the club’s website asone of LAFC’s four primary owners, with Bennett Rosenthal the lead managing partner. Brandon Beck shares a job title with Berg as co-managing owner, while Peter Guber serves as executive chair and owner.Explore more on these topicsMLSUS sportsnewsShareReuse this content

title: Breakout star Alexandra Eala continues rise with first WTA title at DC Open | Tennis | The Guardian
description: Eala staged a remarkable comeback to become the first Filipino player to win a WTA singles title, while Taylor Fritz beat Rafael Jodar in the men’s final
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Eala staged a remarkable comeback to become the first Filipino player to win a WTA singles title, while Taylor Fritz beat Rafael Jodar in the men’s final
Content: Alexandra Eala won the first WTA title of her career on Monday against world No 3 Jessica Pegula at the DC Open.Photograph: Will Oliver/EPAView image in fullscreenAlexandra Eala won the first WTA title of her career on Monday against world No 3 Jessica Pegula at the DC Open.Photograph: Will Oliver/EPATennisBreakout star Alexandra Eala continues rise with first WTA title at DC OpenFilipino sensation beats Jessica Pegula 4-6 6-4 6-0Fritz beats Jodar in men’s final for first title of seasonReutersMon 3 Aug 2026 14.02 EDTLast modified on Mon 3 Aug 2026 16.47 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAlexandra Eala became the first player from the Philippines to win a WTA Tour-level singles title and Taylor Fritz ⁠claimed his first trophy of the season after both rain-delayed DC Open finals were completed on Monday.Eala stunned top seed Jessica Pegula 4-6 6-4 ⁠6-0 after the weather-hit ⁠women’s final resumed ​with the 21-year-old trailing by a set but leading 2-1 in the second, while third-seeded Fritz beat Spanish teenager Rafael Jodar 7-6 (2) 6-4 ⁠in a tight men’s decider.“I feel so much love. My first chance at a title knowing it won’t be the last and already having achieved this milestone for ⁠my career,” Eala said on court. “I knew whatever happened after this match would have already been a ​win for me.”Alexandra Eala is the giantkiller who lit up Wimbledon – but will she rise to the top?Read morePegula, chasing a third Washington title ‌after lifting the trophy in ‌2019 and 2021, was unable to stop the momentum swinging decisively in Eala’s favor.The Filipina won 10 ‌of the 13 games played after the restart, securing the second set before racing through the decider behind a dominant left-handed serve and fearless baseline hitting that drew increasingly vocal support from a partisan crowd despite Pegula playing on home soil.“I want to congratulate Alex on an amazing tournament,” Pegula, the world No 3, said.View image in fullscreenAlexandra Eala celebrates with the DC Open trophy as fans fly the flag of the Philippines behind her.Photograph: Will Oliver/EPA“To see how far you’ve come over the last couple of years ‌when we first played, to see the amazing fans that follow you every place you go, it’s not fun to play against but I think it’s amazing.“The victory extendedEala’s ​winning streak ‌against top-10 opponents​to five matches ​following victories over Elena Rybakina, Elina Svitolina, twice, and Iga Świątek.The breakthrough title will propel Eala to a career-high world No 20 when the new WTA rankings are released.Fritz gets momentum ahead of US OpenView image in fullscreenTaylor Fritz won his first title of the season on Monday in the DC Open final.Photograph: Will Oliver/EPAFritz, meanwhile, captured his first title of the year after edging 19-year-old Jodar in ⁠a contest delayed overnight by the same rain that interrupted the women’s final.Neither ​player dropped serve in the ​opening set before the American dominated the ​tiebreak, then broke early in the second and held firm despite late pressure ​from the Spaniard.The victory ‌gives Fritz momentum heading ​into the Canadian ​Open, the final ATP Masters 1000 event before the US Open. Fritz will again be among the leading American hopes to end the country’s men’s grand slam singles title drought dating back to Andy Roddick’s 2003 triumph in New York.Explore more on these topicsTennisUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Vinícius Júnior to Arsenal doesn’t make sense. That’s why it may work | Soccer | The Guardian
description: Mikel Arteta’s team and the Brazilian star could be a perfect match. It also could be a risk that ends in disaster
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: Mikel Arteta’s team and the Brazilian star could be a perfect match. It also could be a risk that ends in disaster
Content: Mikel Arteta, Vinícius Júnior and José Mourinho.Composite: Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMikel Arteta, Vinícius Júnior and José Mourinho.Composite: Getty ImagesSoccer with Jonathan WilsonSoccerVinícius Júnior to Arsenal doesn’t make sense. That’s why it may workMikel Arteta’s team and the Brazilian star could be a perfect match. It also could be a risk that ends in disasterJonathan WilsonMon 3 Aug 2026 11.00 EDTLast modified on Mon 3 Aug 2026 13.44 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSometimes what is needed is something different.There is a long history in football of counterintuitive thinking being successful, of the benefits of creative tension, of adding grit to the oyster to generate the pearl, but even so, the news that talks betweenVinícius Júniorand Arsenal on personal terms are progressing comes as something of a shock. Mikel Arteta’s great followers of a blueprint adding a free spirit like the Brazilian? Really?Vinícius returns toReal Madridthis week after the World Cup with movement on his future expected relatively soon. He has 12 months remaining on his contract and Madrid are keen either to tie him down to a new deal or to sell him while he will attract at least some kind of fee. As their squad rebuild goes on under José Mourinho, Madrid’s position is readily understandable. They have already signed Bernardo Silva, Denzel Dumfries, Marc Cucurella and Ibrahima Konaté this summer; removing Vinícius’s £420,000 a week (about $30m/year) basic wages significantly increases their financial headroom.The five big beasts are gone: who will be the Premier League’s next alpha manager? | Jonathan WilsonRead moreThere’s been a sense since Kylian Mbappé joined Madrid two years ago that having him and Vinícius together left the squad unbalanced. Why would you need two rapid forwards who both prefer to cut in from the left, particularly when Rodrygo, who tended to be consigned to the right before tearing his ACL in March, would also prefer to play from the left? Yan Diomandé is likely to confirm his move to Real Madrid from RB Leipzig this week. Although the Ivorian has said he would rather play on the right, he too has spent much of his career on the left.More broadly, Vinícius does not seem a natural Mourinho player. His pace and technical excellence are undoubted, but he has never been the most diligent at fulfilling his defensive responsibilities. Mourinho likes a forward who can improvise, and worked successfully with Cristiano Ronaldo at Madrid, but it’s difficult to see how he could indulge more than one such player at a time, and Mbappé will take precedence.But those concerns about tracking, about the willingness to stick to a gameplan, about the capacity to retain possession are just as relevant to Arteta as they are to Mourinho – arguably more so, as Arteta believes far more in structured attacking planning than Mourinho. Is Vinícius, after years of freedom at Madrid, really going to accept those rigid structures?It’s been fairly clear since the second half of last season thatArsenalwould be looking to strengthen their left side. The sale of Leandro Trossard to Beşiktaş did not come as a huge surprise. The 31-year-old is reliable and played a valuable role last season, starting 21 of the 38 league games and coming off the bench on a further 10 occasions, but there is not much stardust about him. Gabriel Martinelli started 11 league games and came off the bench 19 times, and his pace can be a great asset, but it’s no longer clear that he is at his best on the left. The signing of Eberechi Eze last summer looked like an attempt to add creativity from that flank but his tendency to drift infield when Arteta needs his left-sided forward to stay wide meant that by the end of the season he tended to be used centrally behind a striker.Vinícius would give Arsenal greater attacking thrust. At his best, under Carlo Ancelotti, he could transform a game in seconds. His pace, dribbling ability and finishing mean that no matter how stale a game seems to have gone, no matter how under pressure his team may be, they are never more than seven or eight seconds from a potential goal. It’s easy to see why Arsenal are tempted by him. He would immediately be their highest-profile player, adding a sense of direction to a summer that, at least from a recruitment point of view, has seemed to be drifting. Arsenal missed out on Morgan Rogers, who joined Chelsea, while Julián Álvarez, who would seem a much more natural fit on the Arsenal left, appears more likely to go to Barcelona, if sufficient financial levers can be pulled.But the fact Vinícius is not a natural fit may be part of the attraction. It was, after all, the season after signing Erling Haaland, far from a typical Pep Guardiola player, that Manchester City won the treble. A player who does not quite fit, who kicks against the general philosophy, can make a process team less predictable. The friction can produce valuable sparks.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Preview latestEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionHaaland, it’s fair to say, is a different personality from Vinícius and, as a center-forward, there was never a worry he was going to leave his full-back exposed. Vinícius is a bigger risk. He would certainly be an expensive one, not just in terms of his own salary but the inflationary pressure that could have on wages at the club more generally.But he would also add a dash Arsenal have lacked that would make the accusation of being dead-ball plodders hard to sustain. And with Trossard gone, there is a left-sided hole that needs filling.This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian.Subscribe for free here.Explore more on these topicsFootballSoccer with Jonathan WilsonPremier LeagueArsenalReal MadridVinícius JúniorfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: MLS investigates reports of antisemitic chants toward New England’s Dor Turgeman in Montreal | MLS | The Guardian
description: The Israel international scored and gestured toward CF Montéal fans, with the Revolution later saying the ‘strongly condemn’ the chants
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: The Israel international scored and gestured toward CF Montéal fans, with the Revolution later saying the ‘strongly condemn’ the chants
Content: New England striker Dor Turgeman takes a shot against Montréal goalkeeper Sebastian Breza during Saturday’s game.Photograph: Christopher Katsarov/The Canadian Press/APView image in fullscreenNew England striker Dor Turgeman takes a shot against Montréal goalkeeper Sebastian Breza during Saturday’s game.Photograph: Christopher Katsarov/The Canadian Press/APMLSMLS investigates reports of antisemitic chants toward New England’s Dor Turgeman in MontrealIsraeli striker scored, then gestured at CF Montréal fansRevolution ‘strongly condemn’ the chantsJeff RueterMon 3 Aug 2026 17.02 EDTLast modified on Mon 3 Aug 2026 17.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleTheNew England Revolutionhave denounced chants they deemed “antisemitic” and “discriminatory” from CF Montréal fans during Saturday’s MLS matchup between the sides in Quebec. The specific chants were directed towards New England’s Israeli striker Dor Turgeman, with broadcast microphones capturing fans chanting “free Palestine” shortly before he scored a goal.MLS on Monday confirmed it was “aware of reported antisemitic and discriminatory language directed at a New England Revolution player” and that the matter is under investigation.“The Revolution strongly condemn the antisemitic and discriminatory abuse directed at forward Dor Turgeman by CF Montreal supporters during Saturday’s away match,” the club said in a statement issued Monday afternoon. “The club immediately reported the incident to Major League Soccer and has fully supported the investigation. We appreciate MLS’ swift response and commitment to addressing incidents of discrimination. We are hopeful that those responsible will be held accountable for their unacceptable actions.”The scenes in Montreal garnered attention in part due to Turgeman’s response. In the 36th minute, Turgeman scored a tap-in finish to put New England up 2-0. The 22-year-old, who signed for the Revolution last year, stood in front of the home supporters bank with outstretched arms as fans jeered and gestured. Turgeman followed the stance by raising a hand to his ear and walking from end to end of the section with the goal in between him and the crowd. The match ended in a 2-2 draw.In a statement on Sunday, Montréal said the club would investigate the scenes at Stade Saputo.“The club does not tolerate discrimination, or hateful behavior of any kind,” the statement read. “We take these allegations very seriously and are currently reviewing the matter. We are in contact with MLS and the New England Revolution as we work to establish all the facts and take the necessary actions.”After the Hamas attack on Israel in October 2023, MLSbanned both Israeli and Palestinian flagsfrom its venues, with exemptions given in the case of an Israeli or Palestinian player’s presence on a roster. Columbus Crew supporters, for example, were able to display the Palestinian flag after signing Palestine international Wessam Abou Ali in August 2025, but the leaguewide ban remains intact.In February 2025, the league condemned Los Angeles FC investorRuben Gnanalingamfor alleged anti-Israel posts shared on LinkedIn. The Malaysian investor apologized and still retains his stake in the club.Explore more on these topicsMLSUS sportsNew England RevolutionCF MontréalnewsShareReuse this content

title: Serena and Venus Williams set to play doubles in Cincinnati as US Open nears | Tennis | The Guardian

Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The sisters, who last played doubles at the US Open in 2022, could be gearing up for an appearance at this year’s grand slam in New York
Content: Serena and Venus Williams last played doubles in 2022 at the US Open.Photograph: Mike Segar/ReutersView image in fullscreenSerena and Venus Williams last played doubles in 2022 at the US Open.Photograph: Mike Segar/ReutersTennisSerena and Venus Williams set to play doubles in Cincinnati as US Open nearsPair last played doubles at the 2022 US OpenSerena returned to action at Wimbledon before injuryUS Open begins 31 August in New YorkReutersMon 3 Aug 2026 13.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSerena Williams and Venus Williams are ⁠set to make their Cincinnati Open doubles debut this ⁠month after being ⁠awarded ​a wild card on Monday, marking their return ⁠to doubles action for the first time since 2022.The Williams sisters ⁠have won 14 major doubles ​titles, including six ‌at Wimbledon, ‌plus three Olympic gold medals.They last ‌played doubles together at the 2022 US Open, where they lost to Czechs Lucie Hradecka and Linda Noskova.Last month, the sisters had to ‌withdrawfrom the doubles draw at Wimbledon as Serena, 44, ​dealt with a knee injury.The American’s highly anticipated return to grand slam tennis after four years away ⁠was ended at Wimbledon ina first-round ​loss​to Australian youngster ​Maya Joint in the ​singles.
